t: How to Sell Products in Forms
html:
We are excited to introduce new feature Products in Forms to enhance your Forms experience! With this update, users can seamlessly add products to their forms with better customization and layout options.


TABLE OF CONTENTS

  • What to Selling Products in Forms?
  • How to Sell Products in Forms
  • Key Highlights
  • Customizations
  • Tracking payments
  • Email Notifications

What to Selling Products in Forms?


Products in Forms allows you to sell products and collect payments directly through Eleva forms using the Sell Products element. You can add products with images and descriptions, customize their layout, and let customers choose available price levels, variants, and quantities. The feature also supports inventory management, tax calculations, and payment tracking, making it easy to manage purchases through a single form.


What's New
  • Payment Type: Now you have an option to either sell product or collect custom amount from the forms.
  • Ability to select products, include descriptions and images, and choose layouts.
  • Users will also be able to select different variants which are available for the specific product
  • Quantity of product will be respected as per inventory management.
  • Inclusion of tax calculation when someone purchase the product.

How to Sell Products in Forms


The Sell Products element lets you sell products through forms, connect payment providers, and offer multiple price levels and variants.


Important Notes:

• Existing forms and payment configurations continue to work without changes.
• Price levels and variants are available for supported products.
• The enhanced experience supports desktop and mobile devices.


Step 1: Add the Sell Products Element


  1. Go to Sites > Forms.

  2. Under Payments, drag Sell Products element onto your form.

  3. Select the element to open its configuration panel on the right.



Step 2: Configure Payment Providers


  1. Click Connect providers to connect a payment provider directly from the builder.

  2. View connected providers under Connected providers.

  3. Use Manage to access provider settings.

  4. Toggle Live mode to switch between live and test configurations.




Step 4: Customize General Settings


Under the General tab, configure the following as needed:


  • Content: Update the label and its alignment.

  • Address: Add an Address element to your form and enable Billing Address if needed.

  • Coupons: Turn on Enable Coupon and choose its alignment.

  • Footer Info: Customize the footer text or hide it.




Step 5: Add Your Products


  1. Open the Product tab and click Add Product.

  2. Under Choose Product Type, select Main Product.

  3. Choose a product from Select Product. If you haven't created one, click Click here to create it first.

  4. Choose whether to display the product's Description, Image, and Quantity.

  5. Click Add Product to add it to your form.




Step 6: Configure Product Display and Selection


Under the Product tab:

  1. Choose Single Column, Two Column, or Three Column under Layout settings.

  2. Under Product Selection, select Single or Multi to control how many products customers can select.

  3. Adjust Require card for $0 orders to decide whether customers must provide card details for free orders.

  4. To offer an additional product at checkout, configure a Bump Product and turn on Enable Bump.


Step 7: Save and Test Your Form


  1. Click Save to save your changes.

  2. Use Preview to review your form and test the checkout in test mode.

  3. Once everything works as expected, turn on Live mode and save your form again to accept live payments.


Key Highlights

Customizations:

  • You can add up to 20 products
  • Three different layout options are available.
  • These forms can be easily added in the funnels and can be used as one step order form with unlimited customization.

Tracking payments:

  • Upon form submission, the payment amount, order id and payment status are included in the submission details.
  • On clicking Order ID, users will be able order details.
  • These details can also be exported via export options.

Email Notifications:

Email notifications also reflect the status and amount of payment.
Workflow Trigger:
Payment received trigger can be used with "Forms" as source.
Notes:
  • Recurring products are not supported right now.
  • NMI and Authorize.net requires First Name as mandatory field while having payment element in the form.
  • Refund amount will not be captured right now
  • Old way of API based Stripe connect is not supported.
  • In Calendars with custom form payment element, Payment element will not display.
  • Multi payments with Multi native forms not supported in funnel yet
  • Undo/Redo is not supported with Payment element yet
